title: fix(plugin-auth)!: clearing the allowed IP ranges applies at once, and a console save that leaves out the saving address is refused
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgGvhFVhWFL8pKXvjovGpc1g)_

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6Ca3N2EsTAqg7jhabeL

Fixes #30203

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — a settings console save (`PUT /api/settings/auth`) of an `allowed_ip_ranges` list none of whose entries matches the saving request's own address is refused, where it was stored before; and `@objectstack/service-settings` widens its published surface: three new exported types (`SettingsWriteOptions`, `SettingsRequestTransport`, `SettingsWritePredicateOptions`), `setMany`'s fourth parameter accepts `SettingsWriteOptions`, `registerWritePredicate` takes an optional fourth `options`, and `SettingsWritePredicateInput` gains an optional `transport`.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `skills/**` teaches no `allowed_ip_ranges`; `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` describes the setting and does not yet state the save refusal or the recovery, which ship here in the refusal text and this entry (the page is outside this change's surface and is named for a follow-up).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：「允许的 IP 段」清空或恢复默认后立即生效，登录不再被旧列表继续拒绝到重启；在设置页保存一份没有任何一项匹配自己当前地址的列表时，保存被拒，提示里写明你的地址，以及被锁在外面时的救援办法（把环境变量 `OS_AUTH_ALLOWED_IP_RANGES` 设为空值后重启）。
- 为什么改：卡上实测，管理员在家里存了办公室网段，没有任何提示，下次登录才发现进不来；清空字段后页面说已保存，登录却一直 403，只有重启服务器才恢复，业务管理员做不到也看不出原因。
- 风险与回滚：收窄。只影响经设置页（HTTP）保存一份不匹配保存者自己地址的列表这一种操作；能匹配自己地址的列表、清空、启动与种子等进程内写入都不变。判的地址与登录闸门判的是同一个（含 `server.trustProxy` 规则）。回滚即撤本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.ts`（保存时的判定与四种语言的拒绝文案）；`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts` 的 `allowed_ip_ranges` 分支（清空时交回部署自己声明的列表）；`packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts` 的保存路由（把请求的连接交给写谓词，每个谓词只拿到它注册时点名的请求头）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts`，预期 1 个文件、9 条全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**The rule: an allowed-IP list cannot lock out the administrator who saves it, and clearing it applies at once.**

- **Clearing applies at once (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`).** The console sends an emptied field as `null`. The settings cascade then resolves the key with source `default`, and `applySettings` skipped every default-sourced key, so the running `allowedIpRanges` kept the last stored list until a restart. Measured on the real `SettingsService` with the shipped auth manifest: after a `null` save and after `resetNamespace('auth')`, `allowed_ip_ranges` reads `{ value: null, source: 'default' }`. Now a default-sourced value hands the gate back to the deployment's own declaration in the same pass: no list when it declared none, the `allowedIpRanges` the plugin options or an `auth:configure` handler declared otherwise (captured before the manager is built). The reset is applied only when the running list came from a stored setting, so a deployment that never stored one sees no extra config patch. `isExplicit` itself is unchanged.
- **The save is refused (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`).** A settings write predicate on `auth.allowed_ip_ranges` (`allowed-ip-ranges.ts`) refuses a list none of whose entries matches the saving request's address: `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `invalid_value` at the key, `constraint: { clientAddress }`, and a message in the caller's language (en, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES, the settings bundle's locales) that names the address and the recovery. The address is resolved by the auth manager's own `resolveClientAddress` (peer address, or the forwarded one under `server.trustProxy`) and matched by the gate's own `ipMatchesRange`, so the save judges the address the gate later judges. When the address cannot be established, every non-empty list is refused, because the gate refuses that request too. A clear is never refused; an in-process write carries no request and is not judged. The textarea parsing moved into `parseAllowedIpRanges`, shared by the binding and the predicate.
- **The save door carries the request (`@objectstack/service-settings`).** `setMany`'s options become `SettingsWriteOptions` (`SettingsDisplayOptions` plus an optional `transport`: the transport's peer address and the request headers), and a write predicate's input gains the same optional `transport`. The `PUT /api/settings/:namespace` route sets it. It rides the options rather than the caller's context, so the service still receives the resolver's very context (the two door pins that assert identity stay as they are). A predicate sees only the headers it names at registration: `registerWritePredicate(namespace, key, predicate, { requestHeaders })` (`SettingsWritePredicateOptions`), narrowed per predicate in the service, so `cookie`, `authorization` or an API key never reaches one that did not ask for it. The allow-list predicate names the two forwarded-address headers the address rule reads (`FORWARDED_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADERS`, the rule's own list). No `packages/spec` change.
- **Recovery when already locked out.** Every auth key already has a settings env override; `OS_AUTH_ALLOWED_IP_RANGES` set to an empty value is in force (`source: 'env'`), wins over the stored list, and opens the gate on the next boot. The refusal text and the changeset name it. No new env var.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts` (9 cases), on the real `AuthPlugin`, the real `SettingsService` with the shipped auth manifest, and the real settings routes:

- clearing (`null`) opens the gate in the same pass; restoring the namespace defaults does too; a clear returns to the deployment's own declared list, not to none;
- a list without the peer address is refused (status, `code`, field `code`, `constraint.clientAddress`) and nothing is stored; a list that includes it saves and is enforced (preservation);
- under `trustProxy` the forwarded address is judged, and without it the peer address, both ways;
- an address the server cannot establish refuses any list; a clear is never refused and an in-process write is not judged;
- `OS_AUTH_ALLOWED_IP_RANGES=''` opens the gate over a stored list on the next boot.

`packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-write-predicate-transport.test.ts` (3 cases), on the real service and routes: a predicate that named the forwarded-address headers gets exactly those plus the peer address and no `cookie` / `authorization` / `x-api-key`; one that named none gets the peer address and no header; an in-process write carries no `transport`.

<details><summary>Suites and typecheck (head 8767d6aa)</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test`: Test Files 221 passed (221), Tests 3885 passed | 10 skipped (3895).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings test`: Test Files 68 passed (68), Tests 1162 passed (1162).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings typecheck`: exit 0.
- First run of the service-settings suite went red on two door pins (`settings-routes.anonymous-floor.pin.test.ts`, `settings-routes.auth-gate.pin.test.ts`: "the service sees that very context", `toBe` identity) while the transport rode the context; moving it onto the write options turned both green with the pins unchanged.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (each put the forbidden behaviour back through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, saw red, restored; the test resolves both packages from source, so no build sits between)</summary>

- A. the clear branch disabled (`} else if (false /* ABLATION-30203-A */ && …`): 3 failed | 6 passed — the three clearing cases.
- B. the predicate registration disabled: 3 failed | 6 passed — the peer, trustProxy and undetermined refusal cases.
- C. the route's `transport` renamed away: 3 failed | 6 passed — the same three.
- D. the service's forwarding of `transport` to the predicate deleted: 3 failed | 6 passed — the same three.
- After all four (head 4a971127): `git diff HEAD` empty; each restore's blob equals the HEAD blob.
- E (head 8767d6aa). The allow-list predicate registered with `requestHeaders: []`: 1 failed | 8 passed — the trustProxy case (the forwarded address no longer reaches the predicate).
- F (head 8767d6aa). `narrowTransport` passing every header: in `settings-write-predicate-transport.test.ts`, 2 failed | 1 passed — both header cases. After E and F: `git diff HEAD` empty; each restore's blob equals the HEAD blob.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **The same clear-skips bug in other auth keys, not fixed here.** Every `if (isExplicit(key))` branch in `applySettings` without a reset keeps the last stored value after a clear or a restore-default. Measured on the real composition: `lockout_threshold` 3 and `max_concurrent_sessions_per_user` 2 stay in force after both are saved `null`. A general fix needs each key's "deployment declared" value restored, across the refusable `emailAndPassword` pieces that #30201 and #30202 are editing, so this card fixes `allowed_ip_ranges` only and names the family for the seat.
- **The console half.** The field does not show the caller's current address before saving; the refusal carries it (`constraint.clientAddress`) for the console to show. That is the `domain:ui` half, named for the seat.
- **IPv6 ranges.** `ipMatchesRange` matches IPv4 CIDR and exact addresses only, so an IPv6 CIDR entry matches nothing at either door; the refusal therefore says no entry *matches* the address rather than that the list leaves it out. The gap is the seat's to file.
- **The docs half.** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` does not state the save refusal or the recovery override; outside this card's surface, named for the seat.

## Verification

Gates and lint on head `8767d6aa` (the contract-review round, `origin/main` merged in at `89ff3aa9`); the dogfood reading is from `89ff3aa9`.

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 65 commands for the 9 changed paths; each ran with its exit code captured before any pipe.
- `--ran` reconciliation: "65 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 64 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)".
- NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: 35 packages without `dist/`; it needs a whole-workspace build). CI runs it.
- `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`: exit 0 ("48 cases pass"; on the first round it needed `git fetch origin 621a4876…` on the shallow checkout).

</details>

<details><summary>Full dogfood (owed by the (narrowing) arm, head 89ff3aa9): 1 red, from main, not from this change</summary>

- Built the closure, then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` under the verify lock: `VERDICT command-exit 1`, Test Files 1 failed | 418 passed | 3 skipped (422), Tests 1 failed | 3491 passed | 36 skipped (3528).
- The one failure: `test/permission-set-clone-door.dogfood.test.ts` › "a platform set (the lock-and-clone rule's commonest source) copies into its shipping package's pair" answers `422 INVALID_METADATA` (`member_default` clone: "grants on object 'sys_comment' / 'sys_activity' which is not defined in objects") where it expects 200.
- Not this change: the diff touches no permission set, no metadata validation and no clone door. The two grants arrived on `main` with #30222 (`490d136f2`, `member_default` gains `sys_comment` and `sys_activity`), and this test runs only in `main`'s push battery, so it is first seen there. Tracked as #30255 (#30222 reverted by #30262; forward fix in #30310). The contract-review round changes only which headers reach a predicate and the refusal wording, so the dogfood was not re-run on `8767d6aa`.

</details>
